newsitem.title: USA: Triplets and other multiple births rise in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Triplets and other multiple births rise in U.S.

text.p: The number of U.S. women having triplets and other multiple births has more than quadrupled in the past two decades, according to data released on Tuesday.

The National Centre for Health Statistics said the main reason for the dramatic rise was that more women were having babies in their 30s. In addition, older mothers tended to use more fertility drugs and fertility treatments.
In 1994, there were 4,594 multiple births, up from 1,034 in 1971. In 1994, that included 4,233 triplets, 315 quadruplets and 46 quintuplets or greater. The statistics do not count twins.
Multiple births were more common among white women than among blacks. The rate was highest among married college-educated women aged 30 or older.

Babies born in triplet and other multiple births tend to be small and premature and are at a greater risk for health problems. On average, they are half the weight of other babies at birth and arrive seven weeks earlier.
